entities.summary: Marie-Désiré Beaulieu was a French composer and concert organizer who played a crucial role in shaping the country's musical landscape during the Romantic era. Born in Paris in 1791, she rose to prominence in the early 19th century through her innovative compositions and tireless efforts to promote classical music. Her legacy can be seen in the numerous concerts and music festivals she organized, which helped establish Paris as a major cultural hub. Beaulieu's work influenced a generation of French composers, including Hector Berlioz and Charles Gounod, and her contributions to the development of French music are still celebrated today. She died in 1863, leaving behind a body of work that continues to inspire musicians and music lovers around the world. The musical legacy of Marie-Désiré Beaulieu can be seen in the numerous compositions and performances that have been dedicated to her memory, and her influence can be felt in the many concert halls and music institutions that she helped establish. As a testament to her enduring impact, the Paris Opera House still hosts an annual 'Fête de la Musique' in her honor, a celebration of classical music that has become a beloved tradition in the city.
